extension_name: Cookie Editor — View, Edit & Delete Cookies | CookieDesk
extension_description: Inspect, edit, add and delete cookies per site. Search, import/export, partitioned-cookie support. No ads, no tracking.
tile_save_set_title: Save these cookies as a named set file
tile_compare_title: Compare a saved set with now, or two sets
tile_copy_to_title: Copy the shown cookies to another store (normal ↔ incognito)
search_label: Filter cookies by name, value or domain
search_title: Filter by name, value or domain
state_unknown: Click the CookieDesk button in the toolbar to show this tab's cookies.
state_unknown_hint: Chrome shares a tab's address only after that click, or for sites you've allowed.
state_no_access: CookieDesk doesn't have access to $1 yet.
prompt_site: Read and change your data on all $1 sites
prompt_all: Read and change all your data on all websites
only_this_site: Only this site's cookies, nothing else.
restricted_browser: This is a Chrome page. Chrome doesn't let any extension read or change cookies here.
restricted_webstore: This is the Chrome Web Store. Chrome blocks every extension from it, so its cookies can't be shown.

restricted_file: This is a local file. Files opened from disk don't have cookies.

note_no_partitions: Your version of Chrome can't show partitioned cookies, so this list may be incomplete.

hint_httponly: HttpOnly: not visible to page JavaScript (document.cookie can't read it)
hint_samesite_none: SameSite=None: sent on cross-site requests too
hint_samesite_lax: SameSite=Lax: sent on top-level navigations, not on cross-site subrequests
hint_samesite_strict: SameSite=Strict: only sent on same-site requests
row_protect_title: Protect from bulk delete, import and set restore (p)
undo_skipped: Some cookies had already expired and weren't restored: $1.
undo_refused: Chrome no longer accepts these as they were, so they weren't restored: $1.
clipboard_failed: Couldn't copy: the clipboard is not available here.
protected_on: Protected "$1": bulk delete, import and set restore will leave it alone.
protect_limit: You can protect up to $1 cookies. Unprotect some first.
delete_protected_message: This cookie is protected. Delete it anyway? You can undo this.
bulk_match: These cookies match "$1" on $2. You can undo this.
bulk_all: Every cookie listed for $1. You can undo this.
copy_to_default_note: Cookies copied into the Default store are kept like any other cookie, on disk and after this incognito session ends.
copy_to_incognito_note: Cookies copied into an incognito store end with that incognito session.
copy_replace_note: Cookies with the same name, domain and path there are replaced, except protected ones. You can undo the copy.
copy_kept_one: $1 protected cookie there left as it was.
copy_kept_other: $1 protected cookies there left as they were.
copy_undo_hint: Undo it here, or later from the $1 store.
compare_other_site: This set was saved for $1, not $2.
compare_too_many: Pick one set to compare with now, or two sets to compare with each other.
set_file_too_large: $1 is too large to be a cookie set.
import_kept_one: $1 protected cookie left as it was: $2.
import_kept_other: $1 protected cookies left as they were: $2.
import_nothing: Nothing to import: every cookie in the file is already set exactly like that.
rate_text: A quick rating helps others find it.
kofi_confirm_title: Did you buy me a coffee?
kofi_confirm_text: Thank you, it keeps CookieDesk going.
kofi_free: It's free and made by one developer.
host_only_title: Host-only: no Domain attribute, so subdomains don't get it
session_title: Session cookie: gone when the browser closes
httponly_title: HttpOnly: not visible to page JavaScript
no_partition_write: This version of Chrome can't write partitioned cookies.
all_sites_on_text: CookieDesk can read and change cookies on every site, embedded ones included.
all_sites_text: Optional. No more per-site prompts, and cookies of embedded sites (ads, widgets, sign-in frames) show everywhere.
access_lead: CookieDesk sees a site's cookies only after you allow that site, and nothing else: no page content, no history.
all_sites_overrides: All-sites access is on, so these don't matter while it stays on.
privacy_line: No network requests, no cookie values on disk. Undo works for 10 minutes; its copies live in memory and are gone when Chrome closes or the incognito session ends.
export_warning: This file contains live session cookies. Anyone who has it can sign in as you on these sites. Treat it like a password and delete it when you're done.
export_all_one: The cookie listed for $2 goes into the file, even if it is HttpOnly.
export_all_other: All $1 cookies listed for $2 go into the file, including HttpOnly ones.
export_partitioned_left_one: $1 partitioned cookie left out: cookies.txt can't record partitions. Use JSON to keep it.
export_partitioned_left_other: $1 partitioned cookies left out: cookies.txt can't record partitions. Use JSON to keep them.
import_too_big: This file is $1 MB. Cookie exports are far smaller; CookieDesk reads files up to 5 MB.
cant_import_unchanged: Can't import this file. Nothing was changed.
file_unreadable: The file could not be read.
needs_access_one: CookieDesk needs access to $1 more site before it can write these cookies:
needs_access_other: CookieDesk needs access to $1 more sites before it can write these cookies:
import_allow_all_hint: Or allow all sites under Access & settings.
other_sites_warning: This file also writes cookies for sites other than $1. A cookie planted on another site can sign you in to the wrong account there. Only continue if you expected these sites.
also_write_one: Also write cookies for $1 other site
also_write_other: Also write cookies for $1 other sites
import_message_one: Import $1 cookie? Cookies with the same name, domain and path are replaced. You can undo the whole import.
import_message_other: Import $1 cookies? Cookies with the same name, domain and path are replaced. You can undo the whole import.
snippet_warning: The snippet contains live session cookies. Anyone who has it can sign in as you on this site. Treat it like a password.
snippet_paste: Paste it into the DevTools console on $1 to set these cookies there.
snippet_httponly_left_one: $1 HttpOnly cookie left out: page JavaScript can't set it.
snippet_httponly_left_other: $1 HttpOnly cookies left out: page JavaScript can't set them.
set_file_note: The set is a file on your computer; CookieDesk keeps no copy. Restore it later from the menu on $1.
set_too_large: This file is too large to be a cookie set.
cant_restore_unchanged: Can't restore this set. Nothing was changed.
wrong_site_message: This set was saved for $1. Open $1 and restore it there.
foreign_cookies_one: $1 cookie in this file belongs to another site ($2). Restoring a set only changes $3; use Import for other sites.
foreign_cookies_other: $1 cookies in this file belong to other sites ($2). Restoring a set only changes $3; use Import for other sites.
restore_nothing: $1 already matches this set. Nothing to change.
restore_message_one: The cookies of $2 will be replaced by the $1 cookie in this set. You can undo the whole restore.
restore_message_other: The cookies of $2 will be replaced by the $1 cookies in this set. You can undo the whole restore.
err_partition_unsupported: "$1" is a partitioned cookie, which this version of Chrome can't write. Update Chrome to 119 or later.
err_gone: "$1" no longer exists — it may have expired or been changed by the site. Reload the list.
err_not_stored: Chrome accepted "$1" but did not store it.
err_imprecise_delete_one: Chrome can only delete "$2" together with $1 other cookie of the same name, so CookieDesk won't delete it.
err_imprecise_delete_other: Chrome can only delete "$2" together with $1 other cookies of the same name, so CookieDesk won't delete it.
err_irreversible_delete: Chrome no longer accepts "$1" as it is stored, so once deleted it could not be put back. Delete it without undo?
err_no_permission: CookieDesk doesn't have access to $1. Grant access to this site first.
err_secure_shadow: A Secure cookie named "$1" already exists for $2. Chrome won't let a non-Secure cookie with the same name replace or sit beside it. Turn on Secure, or use a different name.
err_rejected: Chrome rejected "$1" without giving a reason. Nothing was changed.
err_irreversible_replace_one: Chrome no longer accepts $2 as it is stored, so once replaced it could not be put back. Continue without undo for it?
err_irreversible_replace_other: Chrome no longer accepts $2 as they are stored, so once replaced they could not be put back. Continue without undo for them?
err_too_large_to_undo: This change touches too much data ($1 KB) to keep an undo copy. Continue without undo?
err_duplicate_in_file: The file contains "$1" twice for the same domain and path.
err_undo_expired: Nothing to undo — undo is kept for 10 minutes.
err_undo_conflict: $1 changed after "$2". Undoing now would overwrite the newer value. Undo anyway?
v_bad_draft: The cookie must be an object with name, value, domain and path.
v_name_type: The cookie name must be text.
v_value_type: The cookie value must be text.
v_name_control: The name contains control characters (such as a newline or tab), which cookies cannot hold.
v_name_semicolon: The name contains ";", which would end the cookie early.
v_name_equals: The name contains "=", which separates the name from the value in a cookie.
v_value_control: The value contains control characters (such as a newline or tab), which cookies cannot hold.
v_value_semicolon: The value contains ";", which would end the cookie early. Encode it (for example with encodeURIComponent).
v_empty_cookie: A cookie needs a name or a value; both are empty.
v_empty_name: This cookie has an empty name. Some sites and tools handle nameless cookies badly.
v_too_large: Name and value together are $1 bytes (UTF-8); Chrome allows at most $2.
v_path_too_long: The path is longer than $1 bytes.
v_path_chars: The path contains control characters or ";", which cookies cannot hold.
v_domain_empty: The domain is empty. Enter the site the cookie belongs to, for example example.com.
v_domain_too_long: The domain is longer than $1 bytes.
v_domain_invalid: The domain is not a valid host name. Use letters, digits and hyphens separated by dots (internationalised names must be in punycode, like xn--...).
v_domain_leading_dot: A host-only cookie cannot have a leading dot in its domain; the dot means the cookie also applies to subdomains.
v_domain_public_suffix: "$1" is a public suffix (a registry-controlled domain like .com or .co.uk), so browsers refuse cookies that apply to all of it.
v_samesite_none_insecure: SameSite=None cookies must be Secure — Chrome rejects them otherwise. Turn on Secure or choose another SameSite.
v_partitioned_insecure: Partitioned cookies must be Secure — Chrome rejects them otherwise. Turn on Secure or remove the partition.
v_prefix_secure: Cookies named "$1..." must be Secure. Turn on Secure or rename the cookie.
v_host_prefix_domain: Cookies named "__Host-..." must be host-only (no Domain attribute, so no subdomain sharing). Turn on host-only or rename the cookie.
v_host_prefix_path: Cookies named "__Host-..." must have the path "/".
v_bad_expiration: The expiration must be a finite number of seconds since 1970.
v_expired_deletes: Saving with an expiry in the past deletes this cookie.
v_clamped: Chrome limits cookie lifetime to $1 days; a later expiry is shortened when saved.
v_expiration_missing: A non-session cookie needs an expiration date. Pick one or mark the cookie as a session cookie.
v_partition_type: The partition key must be an object with a topLevelSite.
v_partition_site_type: The partition's top-level site must be text like https://example.com.
v_partition_site_form: The partition's top-level site must look like https://example.com (https, no path or port).
v_partition_flag: The partition's hasCrossSiteAncestor must be true or false.
v_partition_cross_site: The cookie's domain is not on the same site as $1, so Chrome requires hasCrossSiteAncestor to be true for it.
v_other_site: This cookie's domain ($1) is outside the current site ($2).
io_bad_samesite: $1: sameSite is not one of no_restriction, lax, strict, unspecified.
io_partition_key: $1: partitionKey must be an object with a text topLevelSite.
io_partition_flag: $1: partitionKey.hasCrossSiteAncestor must be true or false.
io_bad_line: Line $1 is not a cookies.txt entry (expected 7 tab-separated fields, found $2).
io_line_flag_subdomains: Line $1: the subdomains flag must be TRUE or FALSE.
io_line_flag_secure: Line $1: the secure flag must be TRUE or FALSE.
io_line_expiry: Line $1: the expiry must be a whole number of seconds.
io_not_text: The file could not be read as text.
io_too_large: The file is larger than the $1-byte import limit.
io_bad_json: The file looks like JSON but could not be parsed.
io_bad_version: This CookieDesk file has an unsupported version.
io_no_cookie_list: The CookieDesk file has no "cookies" list.
io_unknown_format: This JSON is neither a CookieDesk export nor a list of cookies.
io_too_many: The file has $1 cookies; the limit is $2.
io_duplicate: $1: another entry has the same name, domain, path and partition.
explain_third_party: Set by $1, a different site from $2: a third-party cookie.
explain_third_party_partitioned: Set by $1, a different site from $2: a third-party cookie, kept in the partition of $2.
explain_host_prefix: The __Host- prefix makes Chrome insist on Secure, no Domain attribute and Path=/, so no subdomain can set or replace it.
explain_secure_prefix: The __Secure- prefix makes Chrome accept it only with the Secure flag.
explain_scope_host: Sent only to $1 itself, not to its subdomains.
explain_scope_domain: Sent to $1 and every subdomain of it (such as www.$1).
explain_path_all: Sent with requests for every path on that host.
explain_path_under: Sent only with requests for paths under $1.
explain_not_secure: Not Secure: also sent over plain HTTP, where anyone on the network can read it.
explain_httponly: HttpOnly: not visible to page JavaScript (document.cookie can't read it), which keeps it away from injected scripts.
explain_script_readable: Readable and changeable by any script running on the page.
explain_samesite_none: SameSite=None: may also be sent with cross-site requests (embedded frames, images, requests from other sites), where Chrome allows third-party cookies at all (incognito blocks them by default). That is why it must be Secure.
explain_samesite_lax: SameSite=Lax: sent when you navigate to the site, including from a link on another site, but not with requests other sites' pages make in the background.
explain_samesite_strict: SameSite=Strict: only sent when you are already on the same site. Arriving from a link on another site, the first request goes without it.
explain_samesite_unset: No SameSite attribute: Chrome treats it as Lax.
explain_session: A session cookie: deleted when the browser closes (unless Chrome restores your previous session on startup).
explain_expires: Expires $1. Chrome caps any expiry at 400 days from when the cookie was last set.
explain_partition: Partitioned (CHIPS): stored separately for each top-level site. This copy is only sent while $1 is the site in the address bar.
explain_partition_cross: It is in the cross-site part of that partition (used where another site sits between the page and this cookie's site), kept apart from the same-site part.
explain_partition_same: It is in the same-site part of that partition, kept apart from the cross-site part.
explain_partition_other: The same cookie name under another site is a different cookie.
explain_jwt: The value looks like a JSON Web Token.
explain_jwt_exp: The value looks like a JSON Web Token; the token itself says it expires $1.
explain_size: $1 of the 4096 bytes Chrome allows for name and value together.
